clinical_note:
CLINICAL NOTE

Encounter: Neurology follow-up (outpatient specialty)

SUBJECTIVE:
20-year-old female seen today for neurology follow-up. Known history of seizure disorder (6 weeks ago).
History of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, resolved 5 years ago; this is not an active problem.
Pertinent negatives: no history of anemia; no unintentional weight loss; no chest pain; no shortness of breath at rest.
On initial assessment, patient denies fever at triage. On reassessment later in the encounter, patient reports subjective fevers for the past three days. The later history supersedes the triage report; subjective fevers are present.

MEDICATIONS:
- Levetiracetam 500 mg oral twice daily (current)
- Furosemide 40 mg oral daily (prior medication, not current) 5 years ago, taken in the past, not currently prescribed
- Spironolactone 25 mg oral daily (DISCONTINUED) 3 months ago, discontinued due to intolerance
- Metoprolol succinate 12.5 mg oral daily (DISCONTINUED) 3 months ago, discontinued due to hypotension

ALLERGIES:
- Aspirin - bronchospasm (severe)

VITAL SIGNS:
Blood pressure 119/72 mmHg, Heart rate 80 bpm

LABORATORY RESULTS:
- eGFR 13 mL/min/1.73m2 (today) - CRITICAL LOW [ref 60-120 mL/min/1.73m2]
- BNP 65 pg/mL (2 weeks ago)
- BNP 1202 pg/mL (today) - HIGH [ref 0-100 pg/mL]
BNP has increased from 65 pg/mL (2 weeks ago) to 1202 pg/mL (today).

EXAMINATION AND FINDINGS:
Extremities warm and well perfused; alert and oriented.

CLINICAL COURSE:
- Spironolactone discontinued 3 months ago due to intolerance.
- Metoprolol succinate discontinued 3 months ago due to hypotension.
- Panic-range eGFR identified: eGFR 13 mL/min/1.73m2.

ASSESSMENT:
1. Seizure disorder (primary)

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
Constitutional, cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, musculoskeletal, neurologic, and psychiatric systems reviewed and negative except as documented above.

INTERVAL NOTE:
As documented above, extremities warm and well perfused.
